current_f2_context.novel_gap: Current risk coverage does not bind slot save/restore API success fields to an effective post-restart recurrent-state witness.

external_primary_evidence.claim: The slot save/restore API reports n_saved/n_written and n_restored/n_read as operation results.
A Qwen3.5-9B hybrid/recurrent reproduction reports restore reading the saved file and returning n_restored while the following request starts with cache_n=0 and fully re-prefills.
A separate hybrid/recurrent reproduction reports save/restore success counts while prompt reuse is lost after restore because recurrent checkpoints are not effectively persisted.
A Qwen3.5/DeltaNet persistence report describes non-empty slot files but loss of recurrent state and forced full prompt reprocessing after restore.

architecture_delta.name: RESTORE_EFFECTIVE_STATE_WITNESS/v1
architecture_delta.decision: Treat slot save/restore return counts as serialization/transport receipts only. They must not grant effective accelerator-state restoration, latency-recovery, or recurrent-state credit without a post-restore behavioral/performance witness.
architecture_delta.authority_boundary: Conversation transcript, canonical state, decisions and effects remain outside llama.cpp slot state. KV/SSM/DeltaNet state is a rebuildable runtime projection/optimization only.

credit_split.SERIALIZATION_RECEIPT: n_saved/n_written/n_restored/n_read and saved artifact identity only
credit_split.LOGICAL_CONVERSATION_RECOVERY: same canonical transcript/state can produce an admissible next turn, including by full deterministic replay
credit_split.COMPUTE_STATE_RESTORE: post-restart probe demonstrates actual reusable model state rather than full re-prefill
credit_split.LATENCY_RECOVERY: post-restore TTFT/prefill cost remains inside declared voice-session budget

hypothesis: For hybrid Qwen3.5 on some llama.cpp builds, the slot restore receipt can be syntactically successful while recurrent compute state is ineffective, making receipt-only recovery acceptance falsely positive.
counterhypothesis: Frankenstein does not require persisted KV/SSM state for correctness; replaying the canonical transcript after restart may be safer and sufficiently fast for short German voice sessions, so slot persistence can remain an optional accelerator optimization.

probe_sequence: A: cold deterministic multi-turn prefix; record prompt_n/cache_n, TTFT and logs
B: save occupied slot; hash slot artifact; record n_saved/n_written
C: restart server; restore same slot; record n_restored/n_read
D: send byte-identical continuation pinned to restored slot; record prompt_n/cache_n, TTFT and forced-full-reprocessing warnings
E: repeat with transcript replay but no slot restore as the correctness/control baseline
F: repeat at short, medium and long voice-history lengths
cheapest_high_information_falsifier.accept_compute_restore_only_if: Post-restart D demonstrates material prefix-state reuse relative to E/cold and no evidence of full-prefix recomputation under the declared runtime semantics.
cheapest_high_information_falsifier.accept_logical_recovery_if: Canonical replay yields the intended next-turn behavior even if compute-state restore fails.
cheapest_high_information_falsifier.reject_latency_recovery_if: Full replay or ineffective restore violates the declared German voice TTFT budget at any required history length.

recommended_f2_policy: Do not make llama.cpp slot state a truth or memory authority.
Prefer canonical transcript/state replay as the correctness recovery path.
Use slot restore only as a measured optimization after RESTORE_EFFECTIVE_STATE_WITNESS/v1 passes at exact model/runtime identity.
Version-bind any positive compute-state restore credit to model artifact, llama.cpp build, cache configuration and chat template.
